sections.what_happened: ATTRIBUTED REPORT: Eisenkot's Yashar party warned that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was preparing to challenge Tuesday's election results by claiming they were being stolen: 'Netanyahu is in a panic -- and he's laying the groundwork to challenge the results. We have to be ahead of Likud by a huge margin; only then will there be no room to sow doubt about the results.' No Netanyahu/Likud response to this specific warning appeared in the liveblog item.
sections.what_verified: Single carrying family (Gulf News liveblog, T3) relaying the party's own statement; the party is the primary source of its own warning, so the statement itself is the story and no second family is required for the statement -- but the underlying prediction (that Netanyahu will challenge results) is unproven and uncorroborated.
sections.what_disputed: No Likud/Netanyahu response in the item; no evidence offered that results will be challenged; final polls (Haaretz collation via Al Jazeera explainer, Oct 27) put neither bloc at the 61-seat majority, so a contested/negotiated outcome is plausible but not established.
sections.why_matters: 'PANIC OR PREPARATION?': on election day itself, Eisenkot's party accuses Netanyahu of laying groundwork to dispute the result -- the warning, the missing response, and the 61-seat maths (neither bloc projected there) on screen.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Gulf News liveblog 17:46 ; in no prior scan as its own item) -- Yashar party warns Netanyahu is 'laying the groundwork to challenge the results' of Tuesday's election
